title: Assignment bounds — the repository's owner bounds each phase's model and effort per part of the code, and lint holds plans to them

ground.note: Abandoned 2026-10-20. Its goal survives: the owner bounds a phase's model and effort per group of files, and lint flags an unstated departure. Its lint findings are reused. Its separate `phax.planning.json`, `phax planning sync`, planning provider, unfilled entries and price-based model order are dropped.

Approved. §5.2–§5.9 add a per-phase `modelReason`, which is required, a string or null, and placed with `model` and `effort` as the last three keys. It is rendered as `**Model reason:**` and never extracted. §5.17–§5.30 add `phax architecture [path]...` and the `architecture-request` / `architecture-report` formats. Q2 chose the per-phase field. Q3 chose pull. Q4: no provider means one stdout line and exit 1. Q6 made the report a Markdown body only.

A phase ends with `commit`, `modelReason` (NullOr NonEmptyString, described as the departure from the skill's default), `model`, `effort`. `projectExtractedPlan` copies only the extracted fields, so `modelReason` never reaches `phax-plan.json`.
Renders `**Recommended model:**` and `**Recommended effort:**`, then `**Model reason:** <text>` when `modelReason` is non-null, directly under the phase heading.
PHASE_MODEL_POLICY: default `claude-sonnet-5-5` at `medium`, stronger `claude-opus-5-5`, lighter `claude-haiku-5-5`. It is guidance rendered into the skill and never applied to a phase.

Read-only, model-free lint over the deterministic parse of plan.md. The `models` check is `modelFindings` against the routing catalog only, like the run preflight. The plan auditor is the one provider lint already spawns. A failing auditor becomes a finding, never an effect error.
LintCheck is structure | files | commands | models | advisory. A `models` finding names the phase and the reason, and today it is always an error.

The shared run preflight set. `phax run` runs it before it names the run, and executePlan runs it again as the resume re-check, so `phax resume` runs it too. Its `phase-models` check calls `preflightPhaseModels`, the function lint's `models` check calls, and refuses with `Model preflight failed: …` and exit 11. Its inputs are `phax-plan.json` and the plan.md the run reads (the run folder's copy on resume), whose phase sections `phase-sections` locates. `phax run --dry-run` returns before it.

Every top-level key is optional. `brief` and `planAuditor` are provider seats whose command is split on whitespace with no shell. The phax.json effort literal is low | medium | high. The user overlay schema (phax.local.json, ~/.phax/config.json) omits `records`.
Merges project < global user < local user per key. `records` is project-only and never overlaid: the precedent for a project-layer-only key.

A plan sidecar stamped below its current stamp is read by the frozen 0.20.0 decoder and lifted with empty preamble questions and `modelReason: null`. A pre-schema sidecar is lifted the same way. Readers refuse an older shape and name `phax artifact migrate-documents`.

The one writer of older sidecars. It rewrites the sidecars and re-rendered bodies, re-seeds the extraction cache and commits exactly the rewritten paths. It reports Approved artifacts whose text changes. It never touches archived or hand-authored artifacts.
0.25.0.schema.json is cut, so the shape that carries `modelReason` is released and renaming it needs a frozen copy and a lift.
A format's shape lives in `next.schema.json` until the cut renames it to the release. A stamp names the release that last changed the format's shape.
Lists, per release, the steps that release asks for. 0.25.0 asks for `phax artifact migrate-documents`. 0.26.0 has no entry yet.

Draft. Adds a required per-phase `mode` (`headless` | `interactive`) to `phax-plan.json` and the plan document, directly after `optionalFilesToEdit`. An interactive phase plans no file to create or edit; its optional files may name what the person is expected to touch. It ships with this spec, in one plan-document lift.
Reopened to Draft on 2026-10-20. It is to be re-authored later, and will then add a required per-phase `oracle` to `phax-plan.json` and the plan document with its own plan-document lift.

context:
Three pieces already exist.

First, the phax-planning skill teaches a phase model policy, generated from one phax constant: `claude-sonnet-5-5` at `medium` by default; a higher effort or `claude-opus-5-5` for a phase that designs what no code shows yet; `claude-haiku-5-5` for a phase that reproduces a pattern a gate checks. Every departure carries a reason. The policy is the same for every repository, and phax never applies it to a phase.

Second, the plan document carries that reason on each phase as `modelReason`, a non-empty string or null. It sits with `model` and `effort` as the phase's last three keys. phax renders a non-null reason as a `**Model reason:**` line under `**Recommended model:**` and `**Recommended effort:**`, and never extracts it. That shape was cut in 0.25.0: its JSON Schema snapshot is published, and `phax artifact migrate-documents` lifts older sidecars to it.

Third, `phax architecture [path]...` asks the `architecture` provider, declared in any config layer, for an architecture report and prints it. The report is `{ $schema, body }`: a Markdown body phax never parses. The provider knows the parts of the code and never names a model. The format is still in the open 0.26.0 `next` snapshot, so its shape can change before the 0.26.0 cut with no frozen copy and no lift. Without a provider, the command prints one line telling the agent to read the code and its documentation, and exits 1.

`phax plans lint` reads plan.md through the deterministic parser. Its `models` check compares each phase's model and effort with the routing catalog only, and never reads the reason line. Lint is model-free, and it already spawns one provider: the plan auditor.

phax.json's top-level keys are optional. They merge across `phax.json`, `phax.local.json` and `~/.phax/config.json`, except `records`, which is project-only. The routing catalog lists each model's efforts in order. It is built in or read from `~/.phax/model-routing.json`, so it can differ between workstations.

The Draft spec `phase-model-assignment`, abandoned on 2026-10-20, wanted the same thing this spec wants: an owner who bounds each phase's model per group of files. It built that with a separate planning file, a sync command fed by a planning provider, and a model order based on price. This spec keeps that goal and its lint findings, and drops the rest.
problem:
Which code deserves which model is a judgment no metric settles. Today that judgment has no owner and no record. A person may know that `src/core/decide/**` needs Opus at medium effort or more, and that the docs are safe with Haiku, but they have nowhere to write it down. The skill's policy is the same for every repository, so no planner reads that person's choice, and `phax plans lint` cannot tell a plan that respects it from one that ignores it.

The architecture provider knows the parts of the code but hands them over only as prose, so nothing can name a part, let alone bind one. The reason a phase carries, `modelReason`, measures a departure from phax's own policy. It has no notion of the owner's bound, and its name ties it to the model although it explains the effort too.

productGoal.statement: The repository's owner writes in phax.json an ordered list of bounds. Each bound gives the model and effort range for one part of the code: a part the architecture report names, or a set of globs. The first bound that matches a phase's planned files governs the phase. The architecture report names the parts as data, beside its prose. The planner reads the bounds in `phax architecture` before it assigns. It gives each phase its governing bound's model at an effort inside the range, or says why on the phase in `assignmentReason`. `phax plans lint` holds every plan to the bounds: a departure with no reason is an error, and a stated departure is a warning that quotes the reason. The run's preflight runs the same check, so `phax run` and `phax resume` refuse to start on exactly the errors lint reports, before any phase runs. phax applies the owner's choice and checks plans against it. It never decides, guesses, ranks or rewrites a model.
productGoal.guidingRule: The repository's owner decides which code gets which model; phax applies that decision, checks plans against it, and never decides, ranks or rewrites a model.

terminology.definition: One entry of the architecture report's `parts`: a stable `id`, a `name` phax shows but never interprets, a one-sentence `description`, and the `globs` of the files it covers. Only the architecture provider produces parts.

One entry of `assignments` in phax.json: a `model` and an effort range `{ min, max }`, over either a part (a part bound) or a set of globs (a globs bound). A bound is named by its position, `assignments[N]`, counted from 0.
`{ "kind": "part", "part", "model", "effort" }`. It covers the files of the part whose `id` is `part`, through the globs the architecture report gives that part. It copies no glob.
`{ "kind": "globs", "globs", "model", "effort" }`. It covers the files its own globs match: a cut finer than the architecture's parts, or one across them. It needs no architecture provider.
`{ "min", "max" }`: two efforts the bound's model offers, with `min` not after `max` in that model's catalog effort order. The range includes both ends.
Every file a phase plans to create, plans to edit, or may optionally edit.

The first bound, in list order, that matches any of a phase's planned files. A phase with no matching bound, or with no planned files, has none. The owner orders bounds from most to least demanding, as in a CODEOWNERS file. phax never reorders them.
A phase whose model is its governing bound's model and whose effort lies within that bound's range. When no bound governs the phase, it conforms when it takes the policy default.
A phase that does not conform. phax never ranks models, so a departure is neither stronger nor lighter: it is only different.
The skill's default phase assignment, `claude-sonnet-5-5` at `medium`, from PHASE_MODEL_POLICY. It stands in for a bound when none governs a phase.

`assignmentReason`, a required key of every plan-document phase, placed just before `model`: why the phase departs, or null when it conforms. It covers the model and the effort together. A plan.md states it as an `**Assignment reason:**` line. It replaces `modelReason` and its `**Model reason:**` line.

requirements.title: The architecture report carries parts
requirements.statement: The system shall read the architecture report as `{ $schema, body, parts }`, with `parts` a list (possibly empty) of parts that each carry exactly `id`, `name`, `description` and `globs`, and shall publish that shape as the `architecture-report` JSON Schema.

requirements.title: A malformed report is unreadable
requirements.statement: IF an architecture report lacks `parts`, carries a key other than `$schema`, `body` and `parts`, repeats a part `id`, or holds a part with an unknown key or an empty `globs` THEN `phax architecture` SHALL print one line naming the architecture provider and the reason, and exit 1.

requirements.title: phax renders the report for the agent
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax architecture` prints an architecture report THE system SHALL render it to Markdown: the body as is, then each part's name, id, description and globs, in the report's order.

requirements.title: Bounds live in phax.json
requirements.statement: WHERE `phax.json` declares `assignments` THE system SHALL read it as a non-empty ordered list of bounds, each exactly a part bound `{ kind: "part", part, model, effort: { min, max } }` or a globs bound `{ kind: "globs", globs, model, effort: { min, max } }`.

requirements.title: A malformed bound is a config error
requirements.statement: IF `assignments` is empty, or a bound has a `kind` other than `part` or `globs`, lacks a key of its variant, carries a key of the other variant or an unknown key, has an empty `globs`, or names an effort outside phax's effort vocabulary THEN loading `phax.json` SHALL fail with exit 2, naming the bound as `assignments[N]` and the field.

requirements.title: Bounds are the repository's, not a workstation's
requirements.statement: IF `assignments` appears in `phax.local.json` or `~/.phax/config.json` THEN loading the config SHALL fail with exit 2, naming that file.

requirements.title: phax validate checks bounds against the catalog
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax validate` runs and `phax.json` declares bounds THE system SHALL refuse with exit 2, naming the bound and the field, any bound whose model the routing catalog does not list, whose `min` or `max` that model does not offer, or whose `min` comes after its `max` in that model's effort order.

requirements.title: The first matching bound governs
requirements.statement: The system shall take as a phase's governing bound the first bound in list order that matches any of the phase's planned files. A globs bound matches through its own globs, and a part bound through its part's globs.

requirements.title: One conformity rule
requirements.statement: The system shall hold a phase conforming to its governing bound when the phase's model is the bound's model and its effort lies within the bound's range in that model's catalog effort order, and departing otherwise, without ordering models.

requirements.title: An unstated departure is an error
requirements.statement: IF a phase departs from its governing bound and carries no `**Assignment reason:**` line THEN `phax plans lint` SHALL report a `models` error for the phase naming the bound, and the run preflight SHALL refuse with the same error.

requirements.title: A stated departure is a warning
requirements.statement: WHEN a phase departs from its governing bound and carries an `**Assignment reason:**` line THE system SHALL report in `phax plans lint` a `models` warning for the phase that names the bound and quotes the reason.

requirements.title: A conforming phase states no reason
requirements.statement: IF a phase conforms to its governing bound and carries an `**Assignment reason:**` line THEN `phax plans lint` SHALL report a `models` warning for the phase naming the bound.

requirements.title: Lint and the run preflight ask the provider for the parts
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax plans lint` runs on a plan that parses, or the run preflight runs, and at least one bound is a part bound THE system SHALL run the architecture provider once, with an architecture request whose `files` is null, and resolve each part bound to the globs of the part its report gives that `id`.

requirements.title: An unresolved part bound is an error
requirements.statement: IF a part bound cannot be resolved, because no architecture provider is configured, the provider fails or prints an unreadable report, or its report carries no part with the bound's `part` id, THEN `phax plans lint` SHALL report one `models` error for each such bound, naming the bound and the cause, the run preflight SHALL refuse with the same errors, and neither SHALL compare any phase with the bounds or with the policy default.

requirements.title: An invalid bound is an error in lint and in the run preflight
requirements.statement: IF a bound names a model the routing catalog does not list, an effort that model does not offer, or a `min` after its `max` THEN `phax plans lint` SHALL report one `models` error naming the bound and the field, the run preflight SHALL refuse with the same error, and neither SHALL compare any phase with the bounds or with the policy default.

requirements.title: Globs bounds need no provider
requirements.statement: WHILE every declared bound is a globs bound THE system SHALL check plans against the bounds in `phax plans lint` and in the run preflight without running the architecture provider, whether or not one is configured.

requirements.title: An unstated departure from the policy default warns
requirements.statement: IF no bound governs a phase, the phase departs from the policy default, and it carries no `**Assignment reason:**` line THEN `phax plans lint` SHALL report a `models` warning for the phase naming the policy default.

requirements.title: A phase at the policy default states no reason
requirements.statement: IF no bound governs a phase, the phase takes the policy default, and it carries an `**Assignment reason:**` line THEN `phax plans lint` SHALL report a `models` warning for the phase naming the policy default.

requirements.title: The model-reason line is refused
requirements.statement: IF a phase in plan.md carries a `**Model reason:**` line THEN `phax plans lint` SHALL report a `models` error for the phase that names `**Assignment reason:**` as the line to write, and the run preflight SHALL refuse with the same error.

requirements.title: One bounds check
requirements.statement: The system shall compute the bounds findings (the resolution of part bounds, the catalog check of every bound, and each phase's governing bound and conformity) in one domain check that `phax plans lint` and the run preflight both call, as lint's `models` check and the run's `phase-models` preflight both call `preflightPhaseModels`.

requirements.title: A run refuses to start on a bounds error
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax run` or `phax resume` runs its preflight and the bounds check reports an error THE system SHALL refuse before any phase starts (for `phax run`, before the run is named), print every error of the check, each naming its phase (or none) and its bound as `assignments[N]`, and exit 11, as the `phase-models` preflight refuses.

requirements.title: Warnings never refuse a run
requirements.statement: WHILE the bounds check reports no error THE system SHALL let the run preflight pass, whatever warnings the check reports, and WHILE `phax.json` declares no bounds the run preflight SHALL run no architecture provider.

requirements.title: The run preflight reads the reason from plan.md
requirements.statement: The run preflight shall read each phase's planned files from `phax-plan.json` and its reason from the `**Assignment reason:**` line in the plan.md the run reads (the run folder's copy on resume), so `phax-plan.json` carries no reason.

requirements.title: The plan document carries assignmentReason
requirements.statement: The plan document shall require on every phase an `assignmentReason` key, a non-empty string or null, shall carry no `modelReason` key, and shall keep `assignmentReason`, `model` and `effort` as the phase's last three keys, in that order.

requirements.title: The reason is rendered
requirements.statement: The system shall render a non-null `assignmentReason` as an `**Assignment reason:**` line directly under the phase's `**Recommended model:**` and `**Recommended effort:**` lines, and shall render no line for a null one.

requirements.title: The reason is not extracted
requirements.statement: The system shall extract neither `assignmentReason` nor the `**Assignment reason:**` line into `phax-plan.json`, and shall project a plan with or without the line to the same extracted plan.

requirements.title: 0.25.0 sidecars are lifted
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax artifact migrate-documents` meets a live plan sidecar stamped at the 0.25.0 plan-document shape THE system SHALL rewrite it at the current shape, carrying each phase's `modelReason` value over as its `assignmentReason`, re-render each `**Model reason:**` line of its plan.md as `**Assignment reason:**`, and commit both files.

requirements.title: Older sidecars lift straight to the current shape
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax artifact migrate-documents` meets a live plan sidecar stamped below 0.25.0 or written before `$schema` THE system SHALL lift it to the current shape with `assignmentReason: null` on every phase.

requirements.title: Readers refuse an unlifted sidecar
requirements.statement: IF a reader other than `phax artifact migrate-documents` meets a plan sidecar below the current plan-document shape THEN it SHALL refuse the sidecar, naming `phax artifact migrate-documents`.

requirements.title: The headless planner is sent to `phax architecture`
requirements.statement: WHERE an architecture provider is configured or `phax.json` declares bounds THE system SHALL state in the headless plan authoring prompt that the planner runs `phax architecture` before cutting phases and assigning models, and that the command prints the bounds when bounds are declared, after the parts or after its no-provider line. The prompt shall list no bound itself.

requirements.title: Neither a provider nor bounds: the prompt is unchanged
requirements.statement: WHERE no architecture provider is configured and `phax.json` declares no bounds THE system SHALL state in the headless plan authoring prompt, as planning-skill-defaults §5.29 does, that no provider is configured and that the planner reads the architecture from the code and its documentation instead.

requirements.title: The session is granted `phax architecture` with bounds too
requirements.statement: WHERE an architecture provider is configured or `phax.json` declares bounds THE system SHALL allow the headless plan authoring session to run `phax architecture`. This revises planning-skill-defaults §5.30, which allowed it only with a provider. With neither, the session is not granted the command, as before.

requirements.title: phax architecture shows the bounds beside the map
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax architecture` prints a report and `phax.json` declares bounds THE system SHALL print every bound in list order after the parts, showing each part bound with its part's name and globs when the report carries that part. No other output of phax lists the bounds.

requirements.title: Bounds are shown without a provider
requirements.statement: IF no architecture provider is configured and `phax.json` declares bounds THEN `phax architecture` SHALL print its no-provider line, then every bound in list order with each part bound marked unresolved, and exit 1. This revises planning-skill-defaults §5.24, the single no-provider line, for that case only.

requirements.title: The skill teaches the conformity rule
requirements.statement: The phax-planning skill shall teach the governing bound, the conformity rule, the policy default as what stands in when no bound governs, and that `assignmentReason` (or the `**Assignment reason:**` line) is null exactly when the phase conforms, and shall no longer name `modelReason` or `**Model reason:**`.

requirements.title: The skill says where the bounds are read
requirements.statement: The phax-planning skill shall tell the planner, headless or interactive, to read the bounds from `phax architecture` before assigning, including when the command exits 1 with its no-provider line, and shall name no other place where the bounds are listed.

requirements.title: Lint and the run preflight check the bounds
requirements.statement: The system shall check plans against the bounds only in `phax plans lint` and in the run preflight, shall author, approve and extract a plan whatever its conformity, the bounds, or the state of the architecture provider, and shall never stop a phase that has started on account of the bounds.

requirements.title: phax never rewrites a model
requirements.statement: The system shall never write, replace or adjust a model or effort that a plan states, nor a bound's model or effort, in lint, validation, rendering, migration, extraction or a run.

requirements.title: The upgrade guide names the step
requirements.statement: The upgrading guide shall carry, under the release that ships the change, a step naming `phax artifact migrate-documents` for plan sidecars, and the renaming of a hand-written plan's `**Model reason:**` lines to `**Assignment reason:**`.

# Headless authoring — output contract

You are authoring the plan `refunds` in a headless session spawned by `phax artifact new plan --headless`.

- Assignment bounds are declared (phax.json `assignments`), and no architecture provider is configured: before cutting phases and assigning models, run `phax architecture`. - Return ONLY a JSON object …

With a provider configured, bounds declared or not, the first bullet reads as today, and the command prints the bounds after the parts when they are declared:
- An architecture provider is configured: before cutting phases, run `phax architecture` …

With neither, the first bullet reads as today:
- No architecture provider is configured: do not run `phax architecture`; read the architecture from the code and its documentation (README, CLAUDE.md or equivalent).

Normative: the prompt sends the planner to `phax architecture` whenever a provider is configured or bounds are declared, and the session is then granted `phax architecture`; with neither, the prompt and the grant are planning-skill-defaults'; the prompt lists no bound, and no provider runs before the session. arbitratedQuestions.question: How does the planner learn the bounds, and what does `phax architecture` show when no provider is configured but bounds are declared?

options.label: Only `phax architecture` shows them: each part with its bound, then the globs bounds; with no provider, the no-provider line followed by the bounds
options.abandons: The headless planner without a provider: its prompt tells it not to run `phax architecture` (planning-skill-defaults §5.29), so it never sees the globs bounds that apply to it.

options.label: Only the headless prompt carries the bounds as declared; the skill points an interactive planner at `assignments` in phax.json
options.abandons: One place where the map and the bounds read together: an interactive planner joins part ids in phax.json to globs in `phax architecture` by hand.

options.label: The prompt carries the bounds as declared, and `phax architecture` prints them after the parts, also after its no-provider line
options.abandons: A single rendering and the one-line no-provider answer: two outputs show the bounds, and `phax architecture` with no provider prints more than its line when bounds are declared, revising planning-skill-defaults §5.24 for that case.

options.label: Only `phax architecture` shows the bounds, after the parts. The headless plan prompt tells the planner to run it whenever an architecture provider or bounds are configured, and the session is granted `phax architecture` in both cases. With bounds but no provider, the command prints its no-provider line, then the bounds, and still exits 1
options.abandons: The single no-provider line when bounds are declared: the command prints more than its line in that case.

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: Each planner gets the bounds where it already looks. The headless planner reads them in its prompt, as declared, so no provider runs before the session (Q3 of planning-skill-defaults stays pull) and globs bounds reach it with no provider at all. An interactive planner runs `phax architecture` before cutting phases, as the skill already says, and sees each part's globs next to its bound. The no-provider line stays first and the exit stays 1, so an agent still reads it as "carry on". The extra lines appear only in a repository that declared bounds, which is exactly where they are needed.

verdict.why: Decided by the operator on 2026-10-20, off the previous menu (against the recommendation, both). The prompt could carry only a part bound's id, not its globs, which only the provider knows, so the planner must run `phax architecture` anyway. One place shows the bounds, and the planner still pulls (planning-skill-defaults Q3). The headless prompt sends the planner to `phax architecture` whenever a provider or bounds are configured, and the session is granted the command in both cases, revising planning-skill-defaults §5.30 (here §5.32). With bounds but no provider, the command prints its no-provider line, then the bounds, and exits 1, revising planning-skill-defaults §5.24 for that case. With neither, the prompt and the grant are as before.
verdict.advocate: The headless planner sees the bounds without running a command, and no second command reaches its read-only session.

arbitratedQuestions.question: How does `phax plans lint` resolve a part bound, whose globs only the architecture provider knows, and what does it report when the provider is missing, fails, or no longer emits the part?

options.label: Lint runs the architecture provider once (`files: null`) when any part bound exists; an unresolved part bound is a `models` error and no phase is compared with the bounds
options.abandons: Lint passing on a workstation without the provider: a teammate who has not installed it, or a provider that is down, gets exit 1 on every plan while a part bound exists, until the provider answers or the owner rewrites the bound as globs.

options.label: Lint runs the provider the same way; an unresolved part bound is a `models` warning, and the bound matches nothing
options.abandons: The guarantee: lint exits 0 on a plan whose phases were never compared with a part bound, and a later bound silently governs the files the unresolved one would have taken.

options.label: Lint never runs the provider; part bounds are guidance in the prompt and in `phax architecture`, and lint checks globs bounds only
options.abandons: Holding plans to part bounds at all: the variant that follows the architecture becomes advice, and an owner who wants enforcement must copy the provider's globs into globs bounds.

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: Lint is the only place bounds are enforced, and failing it stops nothing else: authoring, approval and runs never read the bounds, so autonomy holds. Lint already runs a provider (the plan auditor), and a provider is not a model, so lint stays model-free. Bound order decides which bound governs, so one unresolved bound changes the verdict of every bound below it. That is why lint compares nothing rather than guessing. A teammate without the provider has a local fix: configure it, or ask the owner for a globs bound.

verdict.why: Decided by the operator on 2026-10-20, as recommended: lint runs the architecture provider once when a part bound exists, and an unresolved part bound is a `models` error under which no phase is compared. Under q-validate the run preflight runs the same check, so an unresolved part bound also refuses `phax run` at its start; a teammate without the provider has the same local fix.
verdict.advocate: A teammate without the provider, or a provider that is down, still gets a usable verdict: a warning names the unresolved bound and lint passes, so the rest of the plan's findings are not held hostage to one tool.

arbitratedQuestions.question: When no bound governs a phase, is a departure from the policy default without a reason enforced?

options.label: A `models` error, as for a bound
options.abandons: The owner as the only source of binding choices: phax's own constant fails plans in repositories that declared nothing, and live plans written at the old Opus default fail lint until every phase gains a reason.

options.label: A `models` warning, as is a reason on a phase at the default
options.abandons: A hard check where no bound governs: a departure with no reason still passes lint, with a warning.

options.label: Not checked: the policy stays guidance, as today
options.abandons: Any visible check of the reason outside the bounds: a repository with no bounds gets no word about an Opus phase that says nothing about why.

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: The policy default is phax's guidance, not the owner's choice, so under the guiding rule it may inform but not fail a plan. A warning still makes an unstated departure visible in every repository. An owner who wants the default binding writes a last catch-all globs bound (`["**"]` at `claude-sonnet-5-5`, medium–medium). That turns the warning into an error, and the choice is the owner's.

verdict.why: Decided by the operator on 2026-10-20, as recommended: an unstated departure from the policy default is a `models` warning. phax's own default may inform but not fail a plan; an owner who wants it binding writes a catch-all globs bound. A warning never refuses a run, so a repository with no bounds runs as before.
verdict.advocate: A departure with no reason is the same defect wherever it appears: an error would make every repository say why an Opus phase is Opus.

arbitratedQuestions.question: Does the plan show a phase's governing bound?

options.label: phax renders a `**Governing bound:**` line beside the model lines in a headless plan
options.abandons: A plan body that stays true: the line is computed at render time from phax.json and the provider's parts, so it goes stale when either changes. It needs the provider at authoring time, a push planning-skill-defaults Q3 rejected, and hand-written plans lack it.

options.label: Only lint names the bound, in each finding
options.abandons: Seeing in the plan itself what a departure departs from: a reviewer reads the reason on the phase and runs `phax plans lint` to see the bound.

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: Lint computes the governing bound from the current phax.json and parts every time it runs, so its answer cannot be stale. The reason on the phase is the planner's judgment, and it stays meaningful when a bound moves. A rendered line would need its own staleness check (the abandoned spec's §5.18) and a provider run at authoring time.

verdict.why: Decided by the operator on 2026-10-20, as recommended: only lint names the governing bound, in each finding, so the plan body never goes stale. The warning on a stated departure quotes the reason the phase gives in `assignmentReason`, read from its `**Assignment reason:**` line, as §5.11 says.
verdict.advocate: A reviewer reading the plan sees what each departure departs from, without running lint.

arbitratedQuestions.question: Where is a bound's `model` (and its efforts) checked against the routing catalog?

options.label: When phax.json is decoded, on every command (exit 2)
options.abandons: A phax.json that is valid on every workstation: the catalog is read from ~/.phax/model-routing.json, so a bound naming a model one workstation's catalog lacks makes every phax command exit 2 there, `phax run` included.

options.label: `phax validate` refuses it (exit 2), and `phax plans lint` reports it as a `models` error; other commands decode only the bound's shape
options.abandons: A check on every command: `phax run`, `phax architecture` and authoring load a bound naming `claude-opus-9` without a word, until validate or lint runs.

options.label: Only `phax plans lint` checks it
options.abandons: Catching a typo before any plan is linted: `phax validate` passes a phax.json whose bound names a model no catalog lists.

options.label: `phax validate` refuses a bound whose model or effort the catalog lacks (exit 2); `phax plans lint` and the `phax run` start preflight run the same bounds check, so the run refuses to start on exactly the errors lint reports; other commands decode only the bound's shape
options.abandons: A run that starts whatever the bounds say: a phase departing from its bound without a reason, a bound naming a model this workstation's catalog lacks, or an unresolved part bound (provider missing or failing) now refuses `phax run` before any phase starts.

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: Only lint consumes the bounds, so only lint and the command that exists to check config need the catalog. That keeps the catalog's per-workstation contents from breaking runs, which must stay autonomous. The bound's shape (variant, keys, effort vocabulary) is still refused at decode on every command, so a malformed bound never loads silently.

verdict.why: Decided by the operator on 2026-10-20, off the previous menu (against the recommendation, validate-and-lint). An error lint reports must be the same error at the run's preflight, as the phase models check already is: lint's `models` check and the run's `phase-models` preflight share `preflightPhaseModels`. One domain check computes the bounds findings for both (§5.20), and `phax run` and `phax resume` refuse on its errors with exit 11 before any phase starts (§5.21). A refusal at start stops no running phase, so runs stay autonomous. The preflight reads each phase's reason from the plan.md the run reads, so `phax-plan.json` is unchanged. `phax validate` still refuses a bound the catalog lacks, and other commands decode only the bound's shape.
verdict.advocate: Runs never read the bounds, so a workstation whose catalog or provider differs can still run a plan.

settled: Decided by the operator on 2026-10-20, not to reopen: (1) the architecture report is `{ $schema, body, parts: [{ id, name, description, globs }] }`, and phax renders it to Markdown on the stdout of `phax architecture`, while the request is unchanged; (2) bounds live in phax.json only, in an ordered `assignments` list of two explicit variants, `part` and `globs`, with no planning file, no sync, no second provider, and no provider that proposes bounds; (3) one conformity rule with no model ranking: the first bound in list order that matches any planned file governs; (4) `modelReason` is renamed `assignmentReason`, rendered `**Assignment reason:**`, still among the phase's last three keys, with the 0.25.0 shape frozen and sidecars lifted by `phax artifact migrate-documents`; (5) in lint's `models` check, an unstated departure is an error and a stated one a warning that quotes the reason.

This spec revises spec `planning-skill-defaults`: Q6 (decided body only on 2026-10-19), since the report gains `parts`; §5.19/§5.20, since the body printed as is becomes the report rendered; and, under q-learn, §5.24 (with bounds declared, the no-provider line is followed by the bounds, still exit 1), §5.28/§5.29 (the prompt sends the planner to `phax architecture` when bounds are declared, even without a provider) and §5.30 (the session is granted `phax architecture` when a provider or bounds are configured, not only with a provider). The rendered `## 12. Decision log` names only the verdicts, so these revisions are recorded here.

Decided by the operator on 2026-10-20 (§9b): q-learn `architecture-widened`, off the previous menu (prompt-bounds, prompt-no-bounds, grant-bounds, arch-shows-bounds, arch-no-provider-bounds, skill-where); q-part `spawn-error` (part-resolve, part-unresolved); q-default `warning` (default-unreasoned, default-reason-on-default); q-render `lint-only` (no governing-bound line; the stated-departure warning quotes the `**Assignment reason:**` line); q-validate `validate-lint-preflight`, off the previous menu (validate-catalog, invalid-bound-lint, bounds-check-shared, run-refuses, run-passes, run-reads-plan, and shape-only decode in bounds-shape).

`assignments` is optional at the top level, as every phax.json key is: absent means no bounds. When present it is non-empty, and every key of a bound is required. Bounds effort values use the plan's effort vocabulary, not phax.json's low | medium | high literal.

Lint and the run preflight read a phase's reason from its `**Assignment reason:**` line in plan.md, so headless and hand-written plans are checked the same way. Matching covers the create, edit and optional lists. An interactive phase (interactive-phases) plans no file to create or edit, but its optional files match bounds as any phase's do, so a bound governs it like any phase: its model and effort, which run its headless first turn and its closing turn, are held to that bound, and `assignmentReason` applies as for any phase. Only a phase with no planned file at all has no governing bound and falls under the policy default.

Decided by the operator on 2026-10-20 in the joint phase-shape session with interactive-phases and oracle-phases: (J1) separate keys, never a single `role`: interactive-phases keeps its `mode` (`headless` | `interactive`), and oracle-phases will add its own `oracle`; (J2) `mode` sits directly after `optionalFilesToEdit` in the plan document and in `phax-plan.json`, and plan.md's `**Mode:** interactive` line follows the Recommended model, Recommended effort and `**Assignment reason:**` lines, while `assignmentReason`, `model` and `effort` stay the last three keys; `oracle`'s place is set when oracle-phases is re-authored; (J3) a bound governs an interactive phase through its optional files, as above; (J4) interactive-phases' placement refusals are one domain check that `phax plans lint` and the run preflight both call, the preflight refusing with exit 11, as this spec's bounds check does; (J5) oracle-phases does not ride this release's lift.

`phax-plan.json` and its schema are unchanged by this spec: the run preflight reads each phase's planned files from `phax-plan.json` and its reason from the plan.md the run reads (the run folder's copy on resume), which the `phase-sections` preflight already locates. Runs change only at their start: the preflight reads phax.json's bounds and, when a part bound is declared, runs the architecture provider. Only the plan document and plan.md change shape.

The `**Model reason:**` label error stays lint's: it is a plan-format finding, not a bounds finding, and the run preflight reads only the `**Assignment reason:**` line. A phase whose only reason line carries the old label departs without a reason in both.

The headless plan authoring session on Claude Code is read-only: its reading tools plus the granted command, as PR #148 made it. Granting `phax architecture` when only bounds are configured adds one read-only command to it.
open: The glob dialect. It must be the same for globs bounds and report parts, and it must be documented in both JSON Schemas' descriptions. Choose a matcher, or Node's built-in path glob matching.
The architecture provider's time limit in lint: reuse `phax architecture`'s.
How `phax architecture <path>...` shows a part bound whose part the path-scoped report does not carry.
The exact wording of the lint findings, the validate lines, the rendered report and bounds, the prompt bullet and the skill text.
Which release carries the plan-document change this spec shares with interactive-phases. If it is not 0.26.0, the upgrading step moves with it.
Where the bounds check sits in `RUN_PREFLIGHT_CHECKS`: it reads the phase sections `phase-sections` locates, so after it.

How often a `phax run` invocation runs the architecture provider: `freshRunPreflight` and executePlan's resume re-check both run the shared set, and the spec asks only that their findings agree with lint's.
Whether `phax run --dry-run`, which returns before the preflight, reports the bounds errors as a "Preflight will fail" line, as it does for uncovered commands.
constraints: This spec and `interactive-phases` (per-phase `mode`) change the plan document together. They ship in the same release, with one frozen copy of the 0.25.0 plan-document shape and one lift by `phax artifact migrate-documents`, which carries `modelReason` over as `assignmentReason` and gives every phase `mode: "headless"`. `assignmentReason`, `model` and `effort` stay the last three keys. `oracle-phases` (per-phase `oracle`), reopened to Draft on 2026-10-20, does not ride this lift: it follows later, with its own.

The architecture-report change does not depend on the plan-document change and should be planned first. The 0.26.0 cut waits for it. Otherwise the report's body-only shape is cut as 0.26.0, and the change costs a frozen copy and a lift of the report.

No back-compat shims: `modelReason` is removed and refused as an unknown key in the current shape, an older sidecar is lifted and never read with the key missing, and `**Model reason:**` is a lint error, not an alias.
Explicit per-variant enums: `kind: "part" | "globs"`, each variant with exactly its keys.

Respect the layers. Bounds and the report are decoded through schemas at the boundary. Matching, conformity and the choice of the governing bound are pure domain. The provider runs through the Shell port, and the catalog loads through the existing loader. The CLI holds no logic. `assignments` is project-only, like `records`: absent from the user overlay schema and never merged.

phax stays autonomous: the bounds can refuse a run only at its start (`phax run` or `phax resume`), before any phase runs, as the `phase-models` preflight does, and never stop a phase that has started. A missing or failing provider never stops authoring, and refuses a run's start only when a part bound is declared.
phax never chooses, ranks or rewrites a model: only the planner and the owner write one.
Fixtures and examples are made up (`acme-guard`, `acme-billing`, `src/core/decide/**`, `refunds`).
Tests hold across a release cut: assert `$schema` URLs by format id and the release pattern, never by the running version.

docsPage.reader: A repository owner who wants phax plans to spend strong models only where their code needs them, and wants lint and the run's preflight to hold planners to that choice, together with the author of an architecture provider (such as acme-guard) who supplies the parts.
docsPage.example: Declare the §6 `assignments`: a part bound on `core-decide` at `claude-opus-5-5` medium–high, a globs bound on `src/*/schemas/**`, and a part bound on `docs`. Run `phax architecture` and see the parts, then the bounds. Remove the provider and see the bounds still listed after the no-provider line. Lint a plan: a phase at `claude-sonnet-5-5` under `src/core/decide/**` fails with an error naming `assignments[0]`, and `phax run` refuses to start on the same error with exit 11; adding an `**Assignment reason:**` line turns it into a warning that quotes the reason, and the run starts. A last catch-all `["**"]` bound makes the policy default binding. A provider prints an architecture report with `parts` beside its `body`.
